How a prompt gets a model to work before it answers, and why much of that moved out of the prompt. Note 23 is the base technique; 24 explains it and 33 limits it; 25, 26–29 and 30–31 are ways to sample, structure or revise the working; 32 and 34 say what changes when the model thinks by itself. Read each arrow as a sentence: chain-of-thought works because of written steps.

Which reasoning method?

  • Direct prompt (33): if one slice fails on multi-step work, go down the tree for that slice only.
  • Tool or solver (33): if the failure moves to writing the plan for the tool, keep the tool and improve the plan.
  • Thinking (34): if the rate of cap stops rises, raise the cap or lower effort.
  • 🗳️ Self-consistency (25): if latency or spend can't take N calls, go back to one chain.
  • CoT (23): if the provider adds a thinking control, delete the trigger.

Two more choices, drawn in their owner notes

  • Vote or critique? (30, Compare table). Would one prompt with a verify line do? Yes on most tasks. Otherwise vote when the answer is one comparable value, and critique when "better" has several dimensions. On reasoning tasks, critique needs a signal from outside the model.
  • Up or down? (28). Would a clearer prompt do? If not: background missing means step back; several hops means decompose, in a chain you can inspect.
